chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: It is not permissible for the one praying to pray while in a state of partial ablution, except with a new ablution.
And it is not permissible for him to pray with impure water.
Nor with water that has been used (for purification).

key_terms.الْمُتَوَضِّئٌ: In a state of partial ablution
key_terms.مَاءٍ مُسْتَهْلَكٍ: Water that has been used (for wudu/ghusl)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for the validity of water and ablution in Shia Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) detailed criteria for the validity of prayer, emphasizing that partial or stale *wudu* invalidates the act, while also clarifying the distinction between water that has been used for purification and water that is merely impure. This narration underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the physical purity of the water and the completeness of the ablution are prerequisites for the spiritual acceptance of the prayer, linking ritual hygiene directly to the integrity of worship.
